claim: A consumer who buys goods online can cancel within two weeks of receiving them without having to explain why.
source: Section 31 Consumer Contracts Act — Right of withdrawal. (1) A consumer may withdraw from a distance contract within 14 days without giving any reason. (2) The withdrawal period begins on the day on which the consumer, or a third party indicated by the consumer, acquires physical possession of the goods. (3) The trader shall reimburse all payments received from the consumer, including the costs of delivery, without undue delay and in any event not later than 14 days from the day on which the trader is informed of the withdrawal. (4) Subsection (1) does not apply to goods made to the consumer's specifications or clearly personalised.

claim: An employee with an open-ended contract who has worked for more than two years is entitled to three months' notice from the employer.
source: Section 86 Employment Act — Notice by the employer. (1) The employer may terminate an employment relationship of indefinite duration by written notice. (2) The notice period is one month during the first two years of employment and three months thereafter. (3) Notice given to an employee during pregnancy or parental leave is void unless the labour inspectorate has given its prior written consent.

claim: The claim against the hotel failed because it had reasonable security in place, including electronic locks and a room safe.
source: Supreme Court, Civil Division, judgment of 14 March 2023 (excerpt). A hotel operator is liable for property stolen from a guest's room only if the guest proves that the operator failed to take reasonable security measures. In the present case the hotel had fitted all rooms with electronic key-card locks and provided an in-room safe, which the claimant did not use. The courts below were therefore right to dismiss the claim. The claimant is ordered to pay the costs of the appeal.

claim: A processor that discovers a data breach has to inform the controller promptly.
source: Section 22 Data Protection Act — Notification of a personal data breach. (1) In the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it, notify the breach to the supervisory authority. (2) Notification under subsection (1) is not required where the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons. (3) The processor shall notify the controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach.

claim: The Seller cannot rely on the 30% cap if the claim arises from its fraud or intentional misconduct.
source: Clause 9 — Limitation of liability. 9.1 The aggregate liability of the Seller for all claims for breach of the Warranties shall not exceed 30% of the Purchase Price. 9.2 The Buyer shall notify the Seller in writing of any Warranty claim within 18 months after Closing, giving reasonable details of the claim. 9.3 The limitations in this Clause 9 shall not apply to any claim arising from fraud or wilful misconduct of the Seller.

claim: Driving more than 30 km/h over the speed limit is punishable by a fine of EUR 300 to 800 and a driving ban wherever it happens, not only in built-up areas.
source: Section 24 Road Traffic Offences Act. (1) A driver who exceeds the maximum permitted speed within a built-up area by more than 30 km/h commits an offence punishable by a fine of EUR 300 to 800 and a driving ban of one to three months. (2) Where the driver has already committed an offence under subsection (1) within the preceding two years, the driving ban shall be at least six months.

claim: Before a limited company can be registered, at least 50% of its share capital has to be paid up.
source: Section 7 Companies Act — Share capital. (1) The share capital of a limited liability company shall be at least EUR 10,000. (2) The contribution of each shareholder shall be at least EUR 100. (3) Before the application for registration is filed, at least one half of the share capital must be paid in. (4) Contributions in kind shall be valued by an independent expert, whose report is attached to the application.

claim: The Court of Appeal upheld the non-compete clause because the employer had a legitimate interest in protecting its clients.
source: Court of Appeal, judgment of 2 June 2022 (excerpt). The non-competition clause in the claimant's employment contract is invalid. It prohibited any competing activity for five years after termination, covered the entire territory of the country and provided no compensation for the employee. A post-contractual restriction on competition is enforceable only if it is limited to a reasonable period, which may not exceed two years, and if the employer pays the employee appropriate compensation for its duration.

claim: The supplier owes a penalty of 0.5% of the order value for each week of delay, up to a cap of 10%.
source: Clause 6 — Delivery. 6.1 The Supplier shall deliver the Goods within 30 days of receipt of the Buyer's purchase order. 6.2 For each full week of delay, the Supplier shall pay the Buyer a contractual penalty of 0.5% of the value of the delayed order, up to a maximum of 5% of that value. 6.3 If the delay exceeds 60 days, the Buyer may withdraw from the contract by written notice.
